subject: DPA: legal-hold, proofs-of-residency & backup retention Q&A
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Legal Ops <legalops@acme.com>
Cc: CloudBroker Security <sec@cloudbroker.io>
Date: 2027-05-12 09:02 -0400
Subject: Questions on DPA redlines: legal hold / backups / proof-of-residency

Hi Irene,

Thanks for sending over the DPA redlines. Legal Ops asked for a quick Q&A so we can confirm our position before submitting formal comments. A few items we need clarified from Redwood's side:

1) Legal hold: If Acme places a legal hold that prevents deletion, how does Redwood treat backups and immutable snapshots? Do you have a documented process for suspending normal deletion flows and an SLA for producing a hold confirmation?

2) Proof of residency: We need evidence that certain customer production data and related logs are processed and stored only in the US region. Can you provide an attestation or a standard template that certifies residency for a given customer, and what granularity (resource IDs, cluster names) that covers?

3) Backup retention windows: The current redline proposes 90 days for backups. Our security team is trying to reconcile that with our internal retention taxonomy — would you support a 30/90 compromise depending on dataset and legal hold exceptions? Also: how are backups encrypted and when are backups purged permanently (secure deletion)?

Attached: Acme_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx (tracked changes).

Can we get a short written response to the above and, if possible, a sample proof-of-residency PDF? If this moves forward, Legal Ops would like a 30-minute call with Security next week.

Thanks,
Carlos Vega
Senior Counsel (Contracts)
Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA redlines: legal hold / backups / proof-of-residency

Hi Carlos — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary here and we'll loop in Security and Legal to provide formal redline language.

- Legal hold: Redwood supports customer-initiated holds that pause normal deletion cycles. Holds are applied at the tenant level and observed by our snapshot/backup scheduler; they prevent deletion of backed-up snapshots until the hold is removed. We can provide a hold confirmation email and a time-stamped policy record.

- Proof of residency: We have a standard residency attestation template; it references cluster IDs, region tags, and Kubernetes node pools used for the customer's production workload. I'll attach the template for your review.

- Backup retention: We currently set backup retention to 90 days by default for hosted customers. We'll outline an approach for conditional 30-day windows for specific datasets (e.g., non-production logs) and explain the secure deletion process — including cryptographic erasure where applicable.

I'll put together a short doc for Legal Ops and schedule a call for next week. Looping in internal folks to confirm technical and legal positions.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12 11:30 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Questions on DPA redlines: legal hold / backups / proof-of-residency

Team — forwarding Acme's questions. Requested items and our asks below. They attached redlines; Legal Ops is asking for (1) formal attestation template, (2) clear language around hold behavior for backups/snapshots, and (3) whether we can offer a shorter backup retention for some data classes.

Key constraints to consider:
- We must avoid indefinite retention obligations. Holds should be time-limited with customer-provided justification and internal escalation for legal demands.
- Proof-of-residency must not reveal internal infra diagrams but should reference tenant IDs + region tags and a signature from our compliance team.
- Any change from 90d default increases operational burden; if we grant 30d for certain classes, we need an automated flag and clear billing/ops implications.

Proposal: draft two alternative clauses for Legal to present — one conservative (retain 90 days, holds by exception) and one flexible (30-day rolling for selective data categories with written hold exception process). Please suggest language and any operational caveats.

Thanks,
Irene

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12 14:05 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on DPA redlines: legal hold / backups / proof-of-residency

Irene / team — suggested compromise language below we can share with Acme as a starting point. 

Suggested clause (flexible compromise):
"For Customer Data stored by Redwood, Redwood retains operational backups for a period not to exceed ninety (90) days by default. Upon written request and where operationally feasible, Redwood may agree to a reduced backup retention period of thirty (30) days for designated data sets identified by the Customer. Customer-initiated legal holds will suspend automated deletion of affected Customer Data and backups for the duration of the hold; Redwood will provide a time-stamped confirmation of hold activation and produce exportable snapshots upon reasonable request and subject to Redwood's processing limits. Redwood reserves the right to require a written justification and to apply holds at the tenant scope."
Operational notes:
- We can implement a per-dataset retention flag; the work is moderate but automatable and would be charged as part of a customization addendum.
- For holds, we already persist hold metadata in an audit log; we can extend the hold confirmation to include an export S3 path or support bundle.

I'll also provide a short template for the hold confirmation and the export process.

—Priyom
Sr. Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@acme.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-13 10:22 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA: legal-hold, proofs-of-residency & backup retention Q&A

Carlos / team — thanks for the questions. A couple of legal clarifications and minor edits to the suggested language above:

1) We cannot accept language that leaves the door open to indefinite suspension of deletion without renewal cadence. Recommend: holds are valid for six (6) months and may be renewed by Customer upon written request with justification. Redwood will document activation and renewal dates.

2) Proof-of-residency attestation: we'll provide a signed PDF that lists the geographic region(s), the cluster/resource tags, and the date/time of confirmation. The attestation will state that Redwood's production processing and primary storage for the named tenant occur only within the specified region(s), excluding ephemeral caches and CDN edges used for latency. This will be limited to the level of detail we typically provide in customer attestations.

3) Backup deletion: implement cryptographic key destruction as the mechanism for secure permanent deletion where feasible, and annotate in the DPA that secure deletion may be subject to third-party storage provider constraints.

Suggested redline tweak to Priyom's clause: add a six-month expiry to holds and require written renewal. Also add: "Redwood shall make commercially reasonable efforts to provide a residency attestation within ten (10) business days of a Customer request."

If this is acceptable to Acme, I'll prepare final redline language and the attestation template (signed).

Neha Kapoor
Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

Neha / Irene / Priyom — appreciate the quick turnaround and concrete language. The six-month renewal cadence for holds and the 10-business-day attestation turnaround both sound reasonable to Acme Legal. A couple of follow-ups before we proceed to redline:

- Can you provide the sample attestation (signed PDF) and the hold confirmation template referenced by Priyom? That will let our Legal Ops check internal process alignment.
- For the per-dataset 30-day option: can you outline any change order cost or SLA implications in a short note? If there is a modest one-time implementation fee, we can probably accept it.
- Finally, once we have the final language we'll circulate to our GC for sign-off. Can Redwood send a DocuSign-ready DPA once redlines are agreed?

If possible, let's do a 30-minute call on Monday 2027-05-17 to finalize. Proposed times: 10:00am ET or 2:00pm ET.

Thanks,
